title: Clamp a glued cover plate onto a base plate with a spring clamp while holding it flush
instruction: Glue the dark grey cover plate onto the aluminium base plate on the grey stand. Pick the cover up from the green mat and set it on the base so that all four of its edges are flush with the base's edges, then hold it there by pressing straight down on its back half with one hand. With the other hand, squeeze the orange spring clamp's ribbed grip and black trigger together to open its jaws, take it off the rack, and slide the open jaws over the front edge of the two plates through the notch between the red marks, the lower jaw under the base plate and the upper jaw over the cover. Let go of the clamp so its jaws close on both plates, then take the holding hand away. Do not move the base plate off its white outline.
context: Clamping parts while glue sets is a routine chore in labs and workshops, here bonding a sensor cover onto its base. On wet glue the cover slides easily, and the clamp's pad drags it as the jaws go on, so one hand presses it flush while the other works a sprung tool.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Gluing stand, fixed: grey PLA block 65 x 50 x 45 mm, x 0.280 to 0.345, y -0.065 to -0.015, with a notch 22 mm wide (y -0.051 to -0.029) and 26 mm deep (x 0.280 to 0.306) through its full height at the middle of its front face; red marks 4 x 10 mm on the front face either side of the notch, centred at y -0.024 and -0.056; white lines 2 mm wide and 0.3 mm thick on its top, 1 mm outside the base plate's back edge (x 0.341 to 0.343) and side edges (y -0.017 to -0.019 and -0.061 to -0.063). Base plate, loose: aluminium 60 x 40 x 6 mm, 39 g, flat on the stand, centred at (0.31, -0.04), x 0.280 to 0.340, its front edge flush with the stand's front face; its top is glued, and the two plates slide on each other with friction 0.08 (wet glue). Cover plate, loose: dark grey PLA 60 x 40 x 6 mm, 18 g, flat on a fixed green mat 80 x 60 x 3 mm, both centred at (0.30, 0.12), its length along x. Clamp rack, fixed: steel bar 50 x 40 x 10 mm, x 0.280 to 0.330, y -0.150 to -0.110, underside 41 mm above the table, on a steel block 25 x 40 x 41 mm under its back end (x 0.305 to 0.330). Spring clamp, loose, 35 g, 66 mm long, 12 mm wide and 32 mm tall: an orange nylon frame with a lower jaw 22 x 12 x 5 mm, a back spine 6 mm thick and a top grip 38 mm long behind it; a black slide in the spine carrying the upper jaw 22 x 12 x 5 mm and a trigger under the grip. Grip and trigger each have six ribs 3 mm across and slope up 10 degrees towards their ends. A spring pushes the upper jaw down onto the lower jaw (500 N/m, about 6 N on 12 mm); squeezing grip and trigger together opens the jaws up to 14 mm, no further. Under the upper jaw, a soft black foam pad 22 x 11 mm stands 2.5 mm proud of it, with a rounded nose 10 mm across at the jaw tip; it squashes flat into the jaw at 0.3 N (120 N/m). Fully open, the lower jaw is 11.5 mm from the pad. The pad's friction on the cover is 0.35. It hangs on the rack's front edge, jaws pointing +x and closed 20 mm over it, the front of its spine at x 0.278, centred at y -0.13, the lower jaw's underside 36 mm above the table. No other objects.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest, relative to the base plate. 0 if any base plate corner is more than 10 mm from where it started (the white outline is 1 mm outside it) or the base is tilted more than 10 degrees. The clamp grips both plates if, at its jaw tips, the lower jaw's face is within 1 mm of the base plate's underside and the upper jaw's face within 1 mm of the cover's top, the jaws are open 11 to 13 mm, the tips are at least 8 mm in from the front edge of both plates and fully on them sideways, and the clamp is tilted no more than 10 degrees from the base. 0 if it does not. 0.5 if it does and the cover is misaligned: at any corner, an edge of the cover more than 1.5 mm from the base's edge along x or y, or the cover twisted more than 3 degrees. 1.0 if it does and the cover is flush within 1.5 mm and 3 degrees. In a real trial, check the edges with a straightedge and a 1.5 mm feeler gauge and measure the jaw tips' reach with a ruler.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Squeeze the clamp off and hang it back on the rack, lift the cover off and lay it on the mat, and set the base plate inside its outline, front edge flush with the stand. In a real trial use no glue, or wipe it and reapply.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. Wet glue is modelled as low friction (0.08) between the plates, no viscosity or adhesion, so the clamp's pad drags the cover off flush as the jaws go on unless it is pressed down. The clamp is a frame and a vertical slide with a linear spring, not a pivoted A-clamp; its foam pad is a sprung slide. Parts are solid boxes and cylinders of uniform density.
